## Problem

You are given an integer. Write a function that produces the binary (base-2) representation of that integer.

The problem is delivered on HackerRank, and your solution is checked against a set of test cases the interviewers have prepared ahead of time. Every one of those test cases must pass for the submission to count.

## Interview Notes

* Format: a phone screen run by two interviewers.
* The call opens with a background conversation led by the hiring manager, and then moves on to this coding problem.
* The coding portion takes place on HackerRank, where the prepared test suite is run against your code; the expectation is that all of the provided tests pass.

## Examples

**Example**

```text
Input: 10
Output: 1010
```

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think of binary as repeatedly asking what the lowest bit of the number is, then discarding that bit and continuing with what remains.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use repeated division by 2 (or bit shifting) to collect remainders, remembering they come out in reverse order of how the result should read.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Watch the edge cases of zero and negative inputs, and confirm what output format the tests expect for them.

</details>
